A fairness label with no valuation is an assertion, not a finding.
recourt_20260805.edge_explainer: MECHANISM (masking x signal x latency): the masking channel is NOT disclosure - it is SUPPLY. On 2026-06-05, one day after the Q1 print and nine sessions after a $51.76 peak, PL signed a $1,500,000,000 ATM equity distribution agreement - 15.4% of diluted market cap - with 14 sales agents and RANGE FORWARD SALE AGREEMENTS with Goldman Sachs Bank USA and Citibank NA, against $730.8M already in cash and an FY27 capex guide of only $80-95M. That is not a funding need; it is opportunistic issuance capacity taken at a record-high stock. SIGNAL CHANNEL: actual usage surfaces only in the quarterly 10-Q financing note / cash-flow 'proceeds from issuance of common stock'. LATENCY: up to ~90 days - and range forwards mean borrowed stock hits the tape BEFORE the company reports issuance. So supply pressure is felt continuously but is ATTRIBUTABLE only quarterly, and the market experiences it as unexplained weakness and prices it as sentiment. GENERALISABLE RULE: an ATM authorised at >10% of market cap, signed within five sessions of a print at/near a 52-week high, against a cash balance that already exceeds multi-year capex, and carrying forward-sale mechanics, is a SUPPLY REGIME, not a financing event - classify the ensuing drawdown as supply-driven (persistent, mean-reversion-resistant), NOT as beta/sentiment (mean-reverting). This is precisely where the prior record erred: it called the drawdown 'mechanical', which implies wait-and-it-comes-back. Beta mean-reverts; a working shelf does not until it is worked through. The 8.4pp of idiosyncratic underperformance and the 6.1pp-lagging bounce are the observable signature.
